title: Knowledge Graphs & GraphRAG: Techniques for Building Effective GenAI Applications: Zach Blumenthal
talk_summary: A hands-on Neo4j workshop building a GraphRAG fashion-recommendation app: load a customer/article/product graph, do vector search, then re-rank results using co-purchase graph patterns and graph embeddings (FastRP + KNN) before feeding an LLM prompt.

takeaways.technique: Two-retriever prompt assembly (search results + inferred recommendations)
takeaways.what_they_do: They run two independent retrievers — a personalized vector+graph search and a graph-embedding recommendation query — and inject both lists into one prompt as separate labeled sections, letting the LLM pick from each.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's going to be sort of two lists that it gets ... tell it to only pick um a certain number from those things

takeaways.technique: Precompute derived text field for embedding
takeaways.what_they_do: Before embedding, they squash several product properties (name, type, group, description) into a single 'text' property and index only that, rather than embedding many fields separately.
takeaways.evidence_quote: creating a new text property to kind of Squish all of that together in one place and we're going to use that um for our upcoming vector

takeaways.technique: Precompute graph-embedding similarity links offline, query at runtime
takeaways.what_they_do: They run FastRP node embeddings + KNN offline and write 'customer also likes' relationships back into the graph, so runtime queries are cheap traversals rather than recomputing similarity.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we've sort of done the KNN beforehand right and we've written the relationships to the graph
takeaways.numbers: FastRP cited as working on graphs with billions of nodes/relationships in ~half an hour

takeaways.technique: Optional-match fallback so retrieval never returns empty
takeaways.what_they_do: The re-ranking query uses an optional match on the peer-group graph, so if no graph signal exists it still returns vector-scored results rather than nothing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's an optional match so ... even if you didn't catch anything in the graph structure you would still have a way to return results based on the vector scoring

takeaways.technique: Rank-based combination instead of naive score multiplication
takeaways.what_they_do: They multiply vector and graph scores as a quick start but explicitly flag it as flawed and suggest rank-ordering or reciprocal-rank-fusion-style combination, validated against labeled outcome data.
takeaways.evidence_quote: just multiplying them together is a good way to get started but is there a better Theory there ... you don't know are they normalized
